title: Value Added Tax VAT In India
definition: Value Added Tax (VAT) is a multi-point destination-based consumption tax levied on the value addition at each stage of the production and distribution supply chain, utilizing an Input Tax Credit (ITC) mechanism to eliminate cascading tax effects.
importanceInUpsc: Crucial for UPSC Civil Services Examination under GS Paper III (Indian Economy - Public Finance, Fiscal Policy, Taxation Reforms, and cooperative federalism leading up to the Goods and Services Tax).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Value Added Tax VAT In India.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Basic understanding of direct and indirect taxes
Fiscal federalism under the Indian Constitution
